summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified. Build: TypeScript compiles clean (tsc --noEmit, zero errors). Tests: 3944/3944 pass across 138 test files, no regressions. AC verification: (1) All 8 routes in buildStoreRoutes() confirmed present and reachable at correct paths. (2) Literal-path routes POST /api/stores/import and PUT /api/stores/order registered before parameterized PUT /api/stores/:storeId regex — first-match-wins dispatch guarantees correct routing. (3) GET /api/stores/conflicts is index 6 in the array, GET /api/stores is index 7, ordering preserved. (4) Section A routes (POST /api/stores, POST /api/stores/import, PUT /api/stores/order, PUT /api/stores/:storeId) have no noBody flag; Section B routes (DELETE, POST :storeId/default, GET /conflicts, GET /) all carry noBody: true. (5) All 6 api-client.js methods present; updateStore, removeStore, setDefaultStore all use encodeURIComponent; addStore/importStore/reorderStores operate on non-parameterized paths. (6) index.html confirmed at api-client.js?v=5. Edge-case review: route dispatch loop verified — string paths use exact equality, regex paths use exec(); DELETE :storeId regex ($) and POST :storeId/default regex (/default$) are disjoint patterns with no conflict.

comments.note: No bugs found. The route ordering implementation is clean and the explicit comments within buildStoreRoutes() (e.g., '-- literal path must precede :storeId routes') serve as self-documenting constraints for future maintainers.

No integration test for the route dispatch ordering exists (e.g., a test asserting PUT /api/stores/order is NOT caught by the :storeId regex). The unit tests in api-stores.test.ts cover handler logic thoroughly, but route registration ordering is untested at the server integration level. Low risk given the deterministic iteration order, but worth noting.

summary: WP-005 code review PASS. The buildStoreRoutes() implementation follows the established sub-builder pattern exactly (same structure as buildRepoRoutes, buildKnowledgeRoutes, buildModelRoutes). All 8 routes are correctly ordered: literal-path routes precede parameterized :storeId routes, GET /api/stores/conflicts precedes the GET /api/stores catch-all. The dispatch mechanism (linear first-match-wins, method filter before path match) confirms the ordering is a load-bearing guarantee, not cosmetic.

Handler call sites in server.ts exactly match the api-stores.ts function signatures: decodeURIComponent applied at the call site for all parameterized storeId routes; ledgerRoot closure capture for handleGetStoresEnriched; body ignored with async () for body-free handlers. statusCode: 201 on POST routes is consistent with buildRepoRoutes precedent.

api-client.js is clean: encodeURIComponent used precisely where needed (updateStore, removeStore, setDefaultStore); addStore/importStore/reorderStores correctly operate on non-parameterized paths. Return type JSDoc is accurate — importStore { stores, warning? } and removeStore { stores, warned } both match the handler signatures. The reorderStores body-wrapping pattern { order: order } correctly matches the server's expected schema.

No blocking issues found. One documentation-forward tagged for api-stores.ts. QA's coverage-gap observation (route dispatch ordering untested at integration level) is noted as a low-risk future enhancement.

comments.note: buildStoreRoutes() correctly follows the sub-builder pattern established by buildRepoRoutes and buildKnowledgeRoutes. The Section A/B split with inline ordering-constraint comments (e.g. '-- literal path must precede :storeId routes') is exactly the right approach for long-term maintainability — future developers adding routes will see the constraint at the point where it matters.

api-client.js method symmetry is clean: the 6 write methods mirror the 6 write handlers in api-stores.ts one-to-one. encodeURIComponent is applied precisely to the three methods that use parameterized URLs (updateStore, removeStore, setDefaultStore) and omitted where the path is static (addStore, importStore, reorderStores). No under- or over-encoding.

[documentation-forward] api-stores.ts handleGetStoresEnriched() JSDoc does not explain why it takes a ledgerRoot argument (it needs to resolve store paths for the enriched list). A one-line note — e.g. '@param ledgerRoot — used to resolve relative store paths on disk' — would make the parameter's purpose self-evident to future callers without reading the implementation.
